alignments.note: Predicate adjective of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula under rule 20; the explicit subject keeps its own English.
Subject noun of the verbless clause.
Pronominal suffix as possessive under rule 18.
Construct adjective keeps only its own word.
Nomen rectum: the ASV recasts the construct relation with *in*, which belongs to the rectum under rule 19.
The ASV recasts `לִתְבוּנָתוֹ אֵין מִסְפָּר` as *His understanding is infinite*, promoting the preposition's object to the English subject and leaving the `לְ` no word; `unrepresented` under rule 40.
Noun promoted to the English subject.
Pronominal suffix as possessive under rule 18.

One English word carries both the existential negation and the counting noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two share a unit; the construction-supplied copula joins it under rule 20 without defeating that condition. Headed on the negation under rules 23 and 50. The competing reading gives *infinite* to `מִסְפָּר` alone and marks `אַיִן` unrepresented, which rule 30 forbids.
